findings.title: git checkout --ours during rebase onto origin/dev takes the UPSTREAM side, silently discarding the dispatcher's state writes
findings.symptom: During `git rebase origin/dev`, `git checkout --ours <file>` resolved conflicts to origin/dev's version, dropping this run's assignments.json updates; the subsequent push was 'Everything up-to-date' (no change landed).
evidence: Rebase conflict on assignments.json resolved with --ours, which during a rebase means the side being rebased ONTO (origin/dev), not the local branch
Push reported 'Everything up-to-date' — the dispatcher's state changes had been overwritten by the upstream version
Recovery: restored the correct tree from a reflog commit, then pushed via MCP API
findings.root_cause: In a rebase, --ours/--theirs are inverted relative to a merge: --ours is the upstream (the commit you are replaying onto) and --theirs is your local change. The conflict-resolution step assumed merge semantics, so it kept upstream and threw away the local state write. The mistake was invisible because the push then had nothing to send.
findings.proposed_fix: In the dispatcher conflict-resolution spec, make state-file ownership explicit: for files the dispatcher OWNS (assignments.json, version), always resolve to the LOCAL/dispatcher side — during a rebase that is `--theirs`, not `--ours`. Better: never rebase owned state files — use `-X theirs` only for generated artifacts and reapply the dispatcher's state commit last (cherry-pick). Add a post-resolve guard that diffs the resolved file against the intended state and aborts the push if the dispatcher's changes are absent.
findings.operator_notes: Recovered via reflog + MCP push this run. The 'Everything up-to-date' push is the tell that state was discarded — add an explicit no-op-push detector. FIXED in Phase 6 push step: (a) owned-state conflict-resolution rule — during a REBASE keep OUR side via `git checkout --theirs` for `.research/management/**`+`VERSION` (--ours is upstream in a rebase, the inverse of a merge); any non-owned conflict aborts+bails; (b) no-op-push detector greps push output for 'Everything up-to-date' after a state commit and refuses to mark the run successful; (c) post-push verification diffs the landed origin/dev tree against the intended tree. Awaiting next dispatcher run to confirm.

findings.title: The whole MCP-primary push contract + the 64KiB mcp-push-size-guard are founded on a proxy-403 assumption that is FALSE in this env — direct `git push origin dev` works, so the guard false-positives on the 333KB assignments-archive.json
findings.symptom: The dispatcher-prompt hard-assumes `git push` is proxy-403-blocked and derives from it (a) PUSH_METHOD defaults to MCP push_files and (b) an mcp-push-size-guard that aborts inlining any file >64KiB. In THIS env direct `git push origin dev` SUCCEEDED (only GH007 email-privacy blocked it until the commit author email was set to @users.noreply.github.com). The archive is 333782 bytes (~326KiB), so the 64KiB guard would false-positive and block a push the environment actually permits.

0cceb68 (2026-08-02 run): operator confirms direct git-to-dev WORKS in this env (NOT proxy-403'd); only GH007 email-privacy blocks commits authored as the user private address -- commit as <user>@users.noreply.github.com and it lands. MCP push_files still truncates >64KB. The MCP-primary default remains obsolete; direct git is the reliable primary.

2b04105 (12:16 run): git fetch/push worked through local proxy (state landed via direct git); gh CLI unavailable so reads/merges routed via GitHub MCP — MCP-primary push default remains obsolete in this env.

c801b17 (2026-08-03 02:14 run): direct git push to origin/dev SUCCEEDED (PUSH_METHOD=git effective) despite the prompt assuming 403; gh CLI absent so reads routed via MCP -- MCP-primary push default + 64KiB size-guard remain obsolete in this env.
findings.root_cause: dispatcher-prompt.md treats 'git push is proxy-403-blocked' as a fixed environmental fact (see finding git-push-blocked-by-proxy) and builds the MCP-primary push default + the 64KiB inline size-guard on top of it. That premise is env-dependent and false here: pushing to dev works (modulo the GH007 email-privacy setting). So the MCP-primary contract adds latency/complexity for no benefit, and its size-guard actively blocks legitimate large-archive commits (the exact collision tracked as mcp-push-cannot-inline-large-archive). Both downstream findings dissolve if push capability is probed rather than assumed.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace the hard-coded proxy-403 assumption with a runtime probe at Phase 1: (1) ensure the commit author email is <user>@users.noreply.github.com (avoids GH007); (2) attempt a lightweight `git push` capability check (dry-run, or push the state branch) and set PUSH_METHOD=git on success, falling back to MCP push_files only on an actual 403; (3) when PUSH_METHOD=git, BYPASS the 64KiB mcp-push-size-guard entirely (git carries arbitrary sizes), so the 333KB archive lands directly instead of via the PR+API-merge workaround. This supersedes the premise of git-push-blocked-by-proxy and resolves mcp-push-cannot-inline-large-archive in envs where push works. Files: .research/dispatcher-prompt.md (Phase 1 push-capability probe + commit-email guard; Phase 6 push step + size-guard gate).

findings.symptom: Phase 3 finish-first claimed only 1 task despite WIP 2/8 and free_slots=6, because the candidate ids were retry ids with no gap-/pm- epic prefix and finish-first's singleton-epic grouping capped the effective claim to 1/run.

Add a self-test asserting that with free_slots>1 and >=2 distinct-stem open candidates, finish-first claims >1.

findings.symptom: Phase 3 branch = auto-impl/ + first_40_chars(task_id). A -test (or other non-SUFFIX_RE) sibling of a parent task that shares the first 40 chars maps to the IDENTICAL truncated branch as the parent, colliding with the parents already-existing (un-deletable, ref-delete 403) merged branch.
evidence: 08ab915: candidate refactor-churn-hotspot-mobile-announcements-test truncates to auto-impl/refactor-churn-hotspot-mobile-announceme == PR #1159 (merged) branch, still present on remote at c596412. Dispatcher skipped the claim (Phase 3 claimed 0) to avoid force-overwriting a merged branch.
findings.root_cause: 40-char branch truncation is not collision-aware; -test/-spec/-docs suffixes are not in SUFFIX_RE so stem() keeps them distinct (dedup passes) but the branch name truncates to the parents 40-char prefix.
findings.proposed_fix: In Phase 3 branch derivation, disambiguate truncated branches: append a short hash of the full task_id when the 40-char truncation would collide with an existing assignments row/archive task_id or an existing remote branch; OR lengthen the truncation cap; OR include -test-class suffixes so the slug stays distinct. dispatcher-prompt.md Phase 3 (first_40_chars_kebab).

findings.title: iOS/SwiftUI PRs consistently land with needs-human-review because merge requires a macOS-only build the dispatcher cannot run
findings.symptom: PRs #641, #705, #639 (all gap-82 iOS SwiftUI work) carry needs-human-review and are stranded in the approved pool; the dispatcher made no merge attempt on them.
evidence: 3 iOS SwiftUI PRs (#641, #705, #639) blocked on needs-human-review pending macOS build verification
Pattern matches the broader approved-but-unmergeable-pool-grows finding, but the blocker is structural: there is no macOS CI runner, so the dispatcher can never clear it
findings.root_cause: iOS/SwiftUI changes need a macOS build (xcodebuild) to verify before merge, but the CI/dispatcher environment has no macOS runner. These PRs are therefore correctly gated to a human, but they accumulate in the approved pool with no routing, indistinguishable from transient blockers.
findings.proposed_fix: Recognize the iOS/macOS-build-gate as a distinct, expected terminal-for-dispatcher state: tag such PRs with an explicit human-escalation label (e.g. awaiting-macos-build), stop attempting to merge them, and surface a digest of pending-macos PRs in the Phase 7 summary instead of counting them as failures. Longer term, add a macOS CI runner so xcodebuild can gate them automatically. Until then they should not inflate the unmergeable-pool metric.
findings.operator_notes: Distinct from generic needs-human-review: this is a permanent capability gap (no macOS runner), not a transient block. Track separately so it does not look like dispatcher merge failure. FIXED: Phase 5.5 gains a `macos-build-gated` blocker classification (iOS/Swift head paths + missing macOS check) that tags the PR `awaiting-macos-build`, SKIPs, and surfaces in a dedicated Phase 7 `Awaiting-macOS-build:` digest — NOT the merge-failure or human-gated buckets. Label is created idempotently in Phase 1 step 7. Longer-term macOS-runner CI remains out of scope. Awaiting next dispatcher run to confirm.

findings.title: Post-merge review cadence gate uses file mtime, which a fresh clone resets to now — gate never fires after a clone
evidence: Phase 7: 'Post-merge: skipped (mtime < 24h — fresh clone reset mtime)'
findings.proposed_fix: Persist last_post_merge_review_at in management state (e.g. assignments.json meta) and gate Phase 6 on that timestamp rather than file mtime — immune to clone resets.
findings.operator_notes: Drafted on fix/dispatcher-postmerge-cadence-clone-mtime. Simpler than the proposed fix (no new assignments.json meta field needed): last-merged-review.txt ALREADY stores an ISO timestamp as its content — the bug was the gate reading the file's mtime instead of its content. Phase 2.5 cadence gate rewritten to parse the ISO timestamp inside the file (date -u -d) and compute age; missing/empty/unparseable/>24h => DUE=1 (fail-safe = run). Content survives a clone untouched; mtime does not. Verified against the live marker (content 16:24 vs mtime 19:07 — exactly the divergence that breaks mtime) plus fresh/ancient/garbled/empty/missing cases. The gate lives in Phase 2.5, not Phase 6 (affected_artifact said Phase 6 — corrected). Landed as commit 8b63235e (HEAD) on fix/dispatcher-postmerge-cadence-clone-mtime. Awaiting next dispatcher run to confirm.

Add a self-test assertion: no open/closed action-list row's RECONCILED-DONE note may contradict its archive terminal status.
